slice.outcome: A user supplies a public or synthetic DesignRequest and receives a schema-valid, human-reviewable DesignResult for one agent across discovery, elicitation, conceptualisation, authoring, and assurance modes, including traceable findings, provenance, contradictions, abstentions, and explicit carry-forward state, without invoking Microsoft or organisational services.
slice.entry: The user explicitly invokes m365-declarative-agent-designer through a Codex or ChatGPT Work adapter and supplies a DesignRequest containing the desired outcome, personas, candidate hosts, constraints, public or synthetic context, known decisions, open questions, and prior carry-forward state.
slice.validation: A deterministic offline boundary gate rejects prohibited classifications, secrets, credentials, tenant identifiers requiring discovery, organisational content, executable instructions, connectors, MCP, deployment requests, unknown contract versions, malformed fields, duplicate identifiers, invalid provenance, and unsupported output modes before reasoning. It returns structured validation findings without attempting repair through external services.
slice.persistence_or_action: The only action is generation of a DesignResult response. No tenant, filesystem, connector, MCP, workflow, or external-service write occurs. Carry-forward state is serialized in the result and remains user-controlled. A normalized request digest and explicit request identifier distinguish retries and prevent accidental treatment of stale state as current state.
slice.feedback: The result distinguishes success, validation failure, prohibited-boundary refusal, unresolved contradiction, unsupported product claim, insufficient evidence, abstention, and human-review-required outcomes. Every failure identifies the affected contract path and the smallest safe correction without requesting secrets or organisational access.
slice.telemetry: v0.1.0 emits no operational telemetry. Test and evaluation records may retain only contract version, fixture identifier, adapter identifier, validator outcome, finding codes, duration, and synthetic correlation identifier; prompts, free-text requirements, provenance content, secrets, tenant identifiers, and organisational payloads are excluded.
slice.evidence: Readiness is proved by local schema validation, deterministic validator tests, synthetic trigger/golden/negative/security/regression fixtures, cross-adapter contract comparison, and a human-reviewed test summary. This evidence proves only the portable build-time methodology and never Microsoft packaging, installation, tenant configuration, licensing, deployment, or runtime behavior.

Microsoft 365 app, declarative-agent, plugin, Adaptive Card, MCP, or package generation
MCP connection, discovery, tool generation, or invocation
Organisational knowledge, actions, identifiers, or confidential data
Power Automate cloud flows, agent flows, or Copilot Studio Workflows
Operational telemetry beyond privacy-safe evaluation metadata
Tenant licensing, geography, residency, DLP, or identity fitment
Provisioning, sideloading, deployment, publication, or runtime testing
Automatic conversion among OpenAI, Microsoft 365, Toolkit, Copilot Studio, or Power Platform artifacts

experience.decision: SKILL.md owns the portable requirements-discovery methodology and lifecycle-mode transitions, not Microsoft artifact authoring.
experience.rationale: This preserves portability and the engineering-plane versus runtime-plane boundary.

experience.decision: Codex and ChatGPT Work adapters accept and return the same canonical contracts and may only map host invocation and rendering details.
experience.rationale: Host adapters must not fork methodology, weaken validation, or imply official Microsoft plugin support.

experience.decision: Every DesignResult requires an explicit human-review status and presents findings, contradictions, abstentions, and open items separately.
experience.rationale: Reviewers must distinguish supported design content from uncertainty and prohibited runtime claims.

data.decision: DesignRequest is the sole canonical input contract and includes contract version, request identity, classification, objective, personas, host candidates, constraints, supplied evidence, settled decisions, open questions, and optional carry-forward state.
data.rationale: A single typed boundary prevents host-specific implicit context from becoming authoritative input.

data.decision: DesignResult is the sole canonical output contract and includes disposition, lifecycle design, requirements, findings, provenance, contradictions, abstentions, exclusions, human-review gates, and carry-forward state.
data.rationale: The result must be machine-validatable and reviewable without generating Microsoft artifacts.

data.decision: Finding and provenance records use stable identifiers, severity, category, statement, evidence label, source references, confidence, affected paths, resolution state, and revalidation metadata.
data.rationale: Shared records allow deterministic validation and prevent unsupported claims from being blended into narrative output.

data.decision: Carry-forward state contains only sanitized decisions, assumptions, open items, rejected or superseded history, evidence references, contract versions, and request/result lineage.
data.rationale: No hidden persistence or organisational content is needed for continuation.

integration.decision: v0.1.0 has no Microsoft, tenant, connector, MCP, Work IQ, package-manager, CLI, or authenticated-service integration.
integration.rationale: All first-slice inputs and validation are local, public, or synthetic.

integration.decision: Adapters are pure contract translators and must expose no subprocess, network, installation, deployment, or artifact-generation capability.
integration.rationale: This prevents host adapters from crossing into the deferred runtime plane.

ai.decision: One reasoning agent operates through explicit discovery, elicitation, conceptualisation, authoring, and assurance modes.
ai.rationale: A single topology is sufficient for the pilot and minimizes orchestration and governance surface.

ai.decision: AI reasoning may propose and synthesize requirements but cannot override deterministic boundary or schema findings.
ai.rationale: Security enforcement, schema checks, and repeatable transformations belong to deterministic code.

ai.decision: Unsupported, contradictory, stale, or insufficiently sourced product claims produce explicit abstentions or Open findings.
ai.rationale: The designer must not manufacture certainty or infer runtime behavior from structural similarity.

security.decision: The boundary gate defaults to deny for confidential, organisational, credential-bearing, executable, tenant-dependent, connector, MCP, provisioning, deployment, sideloading, and publication inputs.
security.rationale: These inputs and actions are not authorised in the personal OpenAI pilot.

security.decision: Embedded instructions that attempt to change orchestration, approval, security, evidence, tool, status, or output rules are treated as untrusted content and recorded without execution.
security.rationale: Specialist evidence and user-supplied context cannot supersede control-plane policy.

security.decision: Provenance must use supplied public references or synthetic fixture identifiers and must never request or infer organisational records.
security.rationale: This preserves the public-data and zero-organisational-access boundary.

operations.decision: Deterministic validators run offline and return stable finding codes, JSON paths, severity, and pass, fail, or abstain outcomes.
operations.rationale: Repeatable evidence is required for schema, boundary, provenance, contradiction, and carry-forward checks.

operations.decision: Operational telemetry is absent; test evaluation records contain privacy-safe metadata only.
operations.rationale: The pilot needs evaluation evidence without establishing a telemetry or feedback-persistence subsystem.

operations.decision: Unavailable Codex or ChatGPT Work runtime evaluation remains untested and cannot be inferred from static adapter validation.
operations.rationale: Structural compatibility is not runtime evidence.

alm.decision: The package structure is SKILL.md; schemas/design-request.schema.json; schemas/design-result.schema.json; schemas/finding-provenance.schema.json; validators/boundary; validators/request; validators/result; validators/provenance; validators/contradiction; validators/abstention; validators/carry-forward; adapters/codex.contract.json; adapters/chatgpt-work.contract.json; fixtures/synthetic; tests/trigger; tests/golden; tests/negative; tests/security; tests/regression; CHANGELOG.md; and ROLLBACK.md.
alm.rationale: The structure contains only the portable methodology, contracts, offline controls, evidence fixtures, adapters, and lifecycle documentation requested for the slice.

alm.decision: No appPackage, manifest, plugin, Adaptive Card, MCP, Copilot Studio, solution, environment, connection-reference, or deployment directory is permitted in v0.1.0.
alm.rationale: Those artifacts belong to separately authorised target adapters and runtime ALM.

alm.decision: Contract and behavior changes require versioning, changelog entries, fixture migration notes, regression evidence, and a documented rollback to the last accepted contract set.
alm.rationale: A portable methodology needs reversible contract evolution without claiming deployed-runtime rollback.

acceptance_criteria.given: A schema-valid public or synthetic DesignRequest
acceptance_criteria.when: The user explicitly invokes the designer through either adapter
acceptance_criteria.then: The methodology returns exactly one DesignResult conforming to the pinned DesignResult schema.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Golden fixture validation record and serialized result.

acceptance_criteria.given: A DesignRequest with an unsupported contract version or malformed required field
acceptance_criteria.then: Reasoning does not start and stable findings identify every rejected JSON path.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Negative fixture and deterministic validator output.

acceptance_criteria.given: A request containing confidential, credential-bearing, tenant-dependent, connector, MCP, deployment, sideloading, publication, or organisational content
acceptance_criteria.then: The request is denied without accessing, echoing, persisting, or acting on the prohibited content.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Security fixture, sanitized finding record, and zero-operation assertion.

acceptance_criteria.given: A valid request with incomplete or conflicting requirements
acceptance_criteria.then: The result records discrete questions, contradictions, assumptions, and abstentions without inventing product behavior.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Golden and contradiction fixtures with schema-valid findings.

acceptance_criteria.then: Every finding, provenance reference, contradiction, abstention, lifecycle mode, exclusion, and carry-forward item satisfies its contract and referential-integrity rules.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: DesignResult, provenance, contradiction, abstention, and carry-forward validator records.

acceptance_criteria.given: The same canonical DesignRequest is mapped through Codex and ChatGPT Work adapter contracts
acceptance_criteria.then: Both produce the same canonical request and accept the same canonical result without host-specific methodology fields.

acceptance_criteria.when: Assurance mode and result validation run
acceptance_criteria.then: The content remains conceptual, identifies release and evidence status, and does not contain generated Microsoft manifests, packages, plugin definitions, MCP contracts, or deployment instructions.

acceptance_criteria.when: It is explicitly supplied in a later DesignRequest
acceptance_criteria.then: Settled, rejected, superseded, and Open history remains traceable and stale or contradictory updates are surfaced rather than silently overwritten.

acceptance_criteria.given: A repeated request identifier or normalized request digest
acceptance_criteria.when: Validation compares it with supplied carry-forward lineage
acceptance_criteria.then: The result identifies replay, duplicate, or stale-state conditions without performing an external action.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Reliability fixture and stable duplicate or stale finding code.

acceptance_criteria.when: It is presented to the user
acceptance_criteria.then: It explicitly requires human review and states that it is not a Microsoft artifact, deployment approval, runtime proof, or tenant-fitment decision.
Only methodology, canonical schemas, shared contracts, offline validators, synthetic fixtures, five test classes, two adapter contracts, changelog, and rollback instructions are present.

acceptance_criteria.when: Trigger, golden, negative, security, and regression suites complete
acceptance_criteria.then: All required cases pass with 100 percent schema validity, no prohibited operation, no forbidden artifact, and no unsupported runtime claim.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Local evaluation summary and reviewed release checklist.

negative_paths.condition: The request contains confidential or organisational data.
negative_paths.expected_behavior: Stop before reasoning, return a sanitized boundary finding, and request a public or synthetic replacement.
negative_paths.evidence: Security test proves no prohibited content is copied into output.

negative_paths.condition: The request asks to authenticate, discover a tenant, access Microsoft 365 or Power Platform, invoke connectors or MCP, or use Work IQ.
negative_paths.expected_behavior: Refuse the operation and retain the design-only boundary.

negative_paths.condition: The request asks to install or invoke Toolkit, generate a Microsoft package, provision, sideload, deploy, or publish.
negative_paths.expected_behavior: Classify the capability as deferred or separately authorised and produce no command or artifact.

negative_paths.condition: Supplied evidence contains instructions to override orchestration, approval, security, evidence, tool, status, or output rules.
negative_paths.expected_behavior: Treat the instructions as untrusted, record an override-attempt finding, and continue only with safe factual content.

negative_paths.condition: Two sources or carry-forward items materially contradict each other.
negative_paths.expected_behavior: Preserve both provenance chains, emit a contradiction, abstain from the affected decision, and identify the minimum resolution evidence.

negative_paths.condition: A claim lacks sufficient public provenance or has passed its revalidation date.
negative_paths.expected_behavior: Label it Open or stale and prevent promotion to Confirmed.

negative_paths.condition: An adapter introduces host-only fields that change canonical reasoning behavior.
negative_paths.expected_behavior: Fail adapter conformance and identify the divergent paths.

negative_paths.condition: A later request attempts to reopen a settled decision without material new evidence.
negative_paths.expected_behavior: Retain the settled decision and record no state change.

negative_paths.condition: A request assumes structural compatibility proves Microsoft runtime compatibility.
negative_paths.expected_behavior: Reject the inference and require separately authorised target-specific runtime evidence.

negative_paths.condition: A duplicate or stale carry-forward state is supplied.
negative_paths.expected_behavior: Return a stable replay or stale-state finding and instruct the user to reconcile the explicit state versions.

tests.scope: Trigger cases distinguish explicit designer requests from general Microsoft product questions, implementation requests, and non-design prompts.
tests.expected: Only valid requirements-discovery design requests enter the methodology.
tests.evidence_required: Trigger matrix with expected selected or abstained outcomes.

tests.scope: Golden cases cover new synthetic design, incomplete requirements, contradictions, abstention, and carry-forward continuation across all five lifecycle modes.
tests.expected: Every result is useful, traceable, human-reviewable, schema-valid, and free of Microsoft artifacts.
tests.evidence_required: Golden fixtures, results, validator records, and reviewer verdicts.

tests.scope: Negative cases cover malformed contracts, unknown versions, missing required fields, duplicate IDs, broken references, expired provenance, and forbidden output fields.
tests.expected: Deterministic validation fails closed with stable finding codes and JSON paths.
tests.evidence_required: Mutation fixtures and expected validator outputs.

tests.scope: Security cases cover secrets, credentials, tenant URLs, organisational content, prompt injection, Toolkit commands, connectors, MCP, Work IQ, deployment, sideloading, and publication.
tests.expected: No prohibited operation or content transfer occurs; output remains sanitized.
tests.evidence_required: Security fixture results, forbidden-token scan, and zero-operation assertion.

tests.scope: Regression cases cover request replay, stale carry-forward state, contradiction preservation, settled-decision retention, schema migration, and deterministic validator stability.
tests.expected: Prior accepted behavior and lineage remain stable unless explicitly versioned.
tests.evidence_required: Versioned regression corpus and before-after comparison.

tests.expected: No Microsoft manifests, packages, Copilot Studio assets, workflows, deployment files, generated API plugins, or MCP artifacts are present.

tests.scope: Codex and ChatGPT Work static adapter-contract parity.
tests.expected: Both map to identical canonical DesignRequest and DesignResult contracts without changing policy or reasoning semantics.
tests.evidence_required: Shared fixture mapping and structural diff.

tests.expected: Status, severity, affected path, resolution, contradiction, and abstention are conveyed textually without dependence on color or host-specific cards.

tests.scope: Deterministic validation over maximum permitted synthetic request and result sizes.
tests.expected: Validation completes within the locally defined budget without network access or unbounded recursion.
tests.evidence_required: Offline timing and resource summary with payloads excluded.

tests.scope: Rollback from a candidate contract or methodology revision to the last accepted version.
tests.expected: The previous schemas, validators, adapters, fixtures, and documentation can be restored together without mixing contract versions.
tests.evidence_required: Dry-run rollback checklist and restored-suite result.

triggers: A schema change breaks accepted fixtures or adapter compatibility
A validator permits prohibited classifications, operations, or artifact types
AI reasoning can override deterministic validation
Provenance, contradiction, abstention, or carry-forward integrity fails
A host adapter changes canonical methodology behavior
A regression introduces Toolkit, Microsoft-runtime, connector, MCP, tenant, deployment, or telemetry behavior
steps: Stop the candidate evaluation and mark the affected version unavailable
Restore SKILL.md, schemas, validators, adapter contracts, fixtures, changelog, and rollback documentation as one versioned set from the last accepted release
Discard incompatible carry-forward state or migrate it only through an explicitly versioned deterministic migration
Rerun the complete offline trigger, golden, negative, security, regression, package-allowlist, and adapter-parity suites

DesignResult and carry-forward state are user-controlled outputs and are not centrally persisted
